chunks: He said: And Abu Muhammad al-Sayrafi narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn Sulayman from Durays al-Kinasi from Abu Khalid al-Kabli, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, Qarun used to wear red garments, and Pharaoh used to wear black and let his hair hang loose; so Allah sent Moses (peace be upon him) against them. And the sons of so-and-so have worn black and let their hair hang loose, and indeed, Allah the Exalted will destroy them through their namesake.

key_terms.السَّوَاد: Black (color), often associated with the Abbasid dynasty
key_terms.بَنِي فُلَانٍ: The sons of so-and-so, a generic reference often used to denote a specific group without naming them directly
key_terms.بِسَمِيهِمْ: Through their namesake, referring to the person named after the historical figure
key_terms.فِرْعَوْن: Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler of Egypt during Moses' time
key_terms.قَارُون: Qarun (Korah), a wealthy companion of Moses known for his arrogance

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wearing black and loose hair in Shia eschatological narratives?
ai.summary: In the context of refuting the Waqifiya, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) uses the typological parallel of Qarun and Pharaoh to critique the Abbasids ('Bani Fulan'), whose adoption of black dress and loose hair mirrored the arrogance of the former. This hadith underscores the Shia view that divine punishment is often executed through a 'namesake'—here, the Prophet Musa or the Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.)—highlighting the continuity of prophetic authority in dealing with political usurpers.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 31 - Narrated to me Abu Muhammad Sairafi from Husain bin Sulaiman from Zaris Kanasi from Abu Khalid Kabuli that he said: I heard Imam Zainul Abideen (a.s) say:

Qaroon dressed in red and Firon used to dress in black; and he used to leave his hair loose and they fell on the two sides of his head; and Almighty Allah sent Musa (a.s) with prophethood. And the sons of so and so (Bani Abbas) also dress in black; and leave their hair loose and they fall on the sides of their heads; and Almighty Allah will also destroy them through his namesake (Musa).
